title: The kernel of a functional with a unit basis value has one fewer basis vector
statement: Let R be a commutative ring, F an R-module, n a natural number, b a basis of F indexed by Fin n [def-weil-pbc-free-module], ℓ:F→R an R-linear functional and p∈Fin n. If ℓ(b(p)) is a unit, ker ℓ has a basis indexed by Fin(n−1). The zero ring is allowed.

proof.text: Choose the inverse unit u⁻¹ of ℓ(b(p)). Restrict the basis coordinate map to ker ℓ and forget coordinate p, obtaining L:ker ℓ→({k∈Fin n | k≠p}→R).
L is injective: if its value at x is zero, all coordinates of x except p are zero, so x=r b(p). Applying ℓ gives r u=0. Multiplication by u⁻¹ gives r=0 and x=0.

L is surjective: given off-pivot coordinates c, extend them by zero at p and take their inverse image v under b.equivFun. The vector v−(u⁻¹ ℓ(v)) b(p) is in ker ℓ and has coordinates c away from p. The proved bijective linear map L is therefore a linear equivalence. Pull back the standard function-space basis and reindex by finSuccAboveEquiv to Fin(n−1). The case n=0 is impossible because p exists.
